jobs.title: Best man, i
jobs.prompt: a four-panel newspaper comic strip, four equal panels in a single horizontal row with thin black gutters (4 panels). Style: comic strip panel, black brush-pen ink line with muddy early-2000s digital flat colors, rubbery kinetic linework, mid-2000s webcomic look, limited palette, slightly misregistered fills. Cast, the same faces, hair and builds in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 29, thin man, hunched, unshaven, tired bloodshot eyes, ink on his right knuckle; GULLY — aged 30, stocky man with a round face, thick forearms, sleeves pushed up; BARNABY (the dog) — a low-slung terrier and hound mix, long body, short legs, folded velvet ears, wiry white-and-tan coat, gray on the muzzle from 2004, cloudy eyes from 2009, carried from 2010. WOOD usually wears black hoodie open over a faded band tee; the brown chore coat outdoors; dark jeans. GULLY usually wears backwards cap, red plaid flannel; the uncle's black rubber apron over it only behind the counter. Clothes, hair-dos and anything held come from this strip's description, never from the reference sheet; hands are empty unless a panel names what they hold. Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: Monday. Gully asks. He asks the way he asks for the flyer. Wood says yes the way he says yes to the flyer. Maria, behind them, already knew. Panel 1: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flat color, a man in an apron wiping a counter without looking up while speaking to a thin man on a stool, a woman in a county rain shell at a dock doorway, a dog (in this panel: GULLY, WOOD, BARNABY (the dog)). Panel 2: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flat color, close-up of a thin man's face as something lands (in this panel: WOOD). Panel 3: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flat color, a practical woman in a rain shell giving a small head-shake to one man and a nod to another, no words. Panel 4: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flat color, a man in an apron sliding a twenty-dollar bill across a counter to a thin man on a stool (in this panel: GULLY, WOOD). No text, no lettering, no speech balloons, no signature; leave clean space in each panel where balloons would go. Reference @barnaby is the model sheet for BARNABY (the dog): match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @gully_27 is the model sheet for GULLY: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @wood_26 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Match the attached references: @barnaby for the character Barnaby; @gully_27 for the character the strip's Gully at 23-31; @wood_26 for the character Wood at 24-31.
